$comment: Golden-recording request list for spec section S2d5 (OpenAI Chat Completions client -> Codex/Responses upstream). Written by @spec-writer; executed by @oracle-runner-3. Deterministic by construction: every request body is fixed, every mock script is a fixed event list; only the fields listed in dynamic_fields vary.
dynamic_fields: Session-Id / prompt_cache_key derived session UUID (upstream header + body; mask per-case when derived, keep when fixed by the case)
Host, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding (transport-level headers in the upstream wire log)

modes.happy: {"mode":"happy"} (or file absent) — serve the script's canned SSE (the request always carries stream:true, so the SSE branch always serves)
modes.happy+script: {"mode":"happy","script":"<script-name>"} — serve that script's canned SSE (requires the mock extension below)
modes.error: {"mode":"error","status":429} — HTTP 429 + default codex error body {"error":{"message":"mock rate limit","type":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}
modes.disconnect: {"mode":"disconnect","after":5} — serve the CANNED default stream, hard-close (no chunked terminator) after N events

mock_control_protocol.mock_extension_needed: responses_common.py currently hardcodes ONE happy script. Please add a script registry: when control/script (or an X-Mock-Script header, stripped before wire logging) names a script, serve that exact (event,data) list instead. The script lists are in `scripts` below — they are plain JSON, reuse mocklib.send_sse. No other mock change needed. The mock must keep deciding stream-vs-JSON by body.stream (the reference always sends stream:true).

ordering_notes: Run happy/script cases first; 429 and cooldown cases (S2D5-15, -16, -24) last.
Every 429 arms a rate-limit cooldown; the codex window recorded as ~4s (see S2D5-24 notes) — space error-mode cases >=5s apart, EXCEPT inside S2D5-24 where the pair must be back-to-back.

The mock log (mock/logs/codex.jsonl) is truncated on mock start; keep one reference+mock restart for the whole batch and slice per-case wire lines by offsets (recorded batch: one mock start, per-request line counts in meta.yaml).
Port adaptation for the recording stack is captured in each fixture meta.yaml (worker-3 batch: downstream 8397, mock 21003; the spec section §6 documents this).

cases.purpose: After an upstream 429, the credential enters a rate-limit cooldown that transient-error-cooldown-seconds:-1 does NOT disable; the immediate retry gets the model_cooldown error (RECORDED: HTTP 429 + Retry-After, not 500).

ordering: request-b MUST be sent within ~1s after request-a completes (replay back-to-back); if request-b does not show model_cooldown, wait for cooldown reset and re-run the pair
cases.expected_downstream: RECORDED (2026-09-15, oracle-runner-3): request-a: HTTP 429, verbatim mock error body. request-b: HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 4 and body {"error":{"code":"model_cooldown","last_upstream_error":"<VERBATIM 429 body, json.dumps spacing preserved>","message":"All credentials for model cx are cooling down via provider codex (last error: <verbatim 429 body>)","model":"cx","provider":"codex","reset_seconds":4,"reset_time":"4s"}} (alphabetical keys). Recorded R2 omits X-Cpa-Trace-Id. Mask reset_seconds/reset_time/Retry-After/X-Cpa-Trace-Id/Date in meta.yaml dynamic_fields (remaining-window values are time-dependent on replay).
cases.notes: Recorded fixture supersedes the original expected shape (500/summary-form last_upstream_error) — see spec section §5 E2 and §7 items 13-15. Pair must be replayed back-to-back; prior 429 cases must be ≥5s in the past (residual cooldown observed at 1.2s).

recording_status.mock_script_registry: s2d5_scripts.json (generated byte-exactly from this file's scripts object)
recording_status.deviations_from_expectations: S2D5-24: cooldown surfaced as HTTP 429 + Retry-After: 4, reset_seconds/reset_time 4/4s, last_upstream_error VERBATIM body (not summary form), model_cooldown R2 without X-Cpa-Trace-Id — incorporated into spec §5 E2 + §7 items 13-15. recording_status.operational_lesson: Rate-limit cooldown window (~4s for codex) exceeds the gemini wire-note's ~1s; leave >=5s between error-mode cases when re-recording. Request-body claims must be derived from recorded wire logs first (reasoning strip lesson).
